This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.1,50,00,000/- for the death of Hasina @ Hasina Taj in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 31-01-2023 at about 8.00 p.m., the deceased Hasina @ Hasina Taj along with her daughter was walking towards Kinto school, Old Guddadahalli main road,
Bangalore, at that time, the driver of Tayota Glaza car bearing No.KA-53- MJ-1166 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against deceased Hasina @ Hasina Taj and her daughter.
Both fell down and the car wheels ran on the chest of the deceased Hasina @ Hasina Taj.
Due to the impact, the deceased and her daughter sustained severe chest and bodily injuries.

Prior to the accident, said Hasina @ Hasina Taj was hale and healthy and she was working as vegetables and fruits street vendor and was earning a sum of Rs.40,000/-
per month.
Entire family of the deceased were depending on the income of the deceased.
The cause of death is due to accidental injuries.
The said accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tayota Glaza car bearing Reg.No.KA-53- MJ-1166.
The Respondent No.1 is the insurer, respondent No.2 is the owner and the Respondent No.3 is the policy holder of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-MJ-1166.
Therefore, both the Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
3. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.1 and 2 appeared before the Court through their respective counsels and filed their respective written statement.

Respondent No.1 in the Objection Statement to the main petition denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tayota Glaza car and the accident has occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased and her daughter were talking to each other without observing the traffic, suddenly came to the middle of the road, hence contributory negligence is more on the part of the deceased Alla Bakash vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150103006/
3 and her daughter.

sentences.text: Further contended that the petitioners are major, married and earning persons.
Deceased was not at all earning person due to old age and the deceased being looked after by the petitioners.
Further, it denies for having insured Tayota Glaza car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-MJ- 1166 pending confirmation from the concerned branch of the respondent.
Further it contended that the driver of vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Further it contended that owner of the insured car has not intimated the alleged accident to this respondent and there is violation of Section 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act of Motor Vehicles Act.

sentences.text: Further contended that there is no nexus between injuries and death.

On these grounds,
Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

Respondent No.2 filed objection statement to the main petition denying the age, avocation and income of the deceased and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tayota Glaza car and the accident has occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased.
Further he contended that the vehicle is insured with the respondent No.2 and it is in force as on the date of accident.
As such, he is not liable to pay any compensation.
Hence, among these and other grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against him.

4. On the basis of the rival pleadings, the following Issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal representatives of the deceased?
2.

Whether the Petitioners prove that Smt.Hasina @ Hasina Taj died due to injuries sustained by her in an accident occurred on 31.01.2023 at about 8.00 p.m. near Kinto School, 5th Cross, Old Guddadahalli, Vinayaka Nagar, Bengaluru, arising due to rash and negligent driving of Tayota Glaza car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-MJ-1166?
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
4. What award or order?
5. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner No.1 got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 13 documents as per Ex.P.1 to 13 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondents have not chosen to lead evidence.
6. The counsel for the petitioner has relied on the judgment in MFA.No.2591/2019(MV) between Sri.Segaran.V Vs. Smt.Indu.N and another, date of disposal on 27.07.2021.

I have perused the depositions, documents exhibited, the judgment relied by the learned counsel for the petitioner and materials available on record.

8. My answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No. 4 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS  9. Issue No.2: It is the case of the Petitioners that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tayota Glaza car bearing Reg.No.KA- 53-MJ-1166 and in the said accident, Hasina @ Hasina Taj had succumbed to the injuries.
10.
On the other hand, the Respondents have denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tayota Glaza car.

11. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, Petitioner No.1 got examined himself as P.W.1 and he has filed his chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and re-iterated the petition averments.
12. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, PW.1 has relied on Ex.P-1 to Ex.P13.

Ex.P-1 and 2 are the certified copy of FIR and complaint, which show that Magadi Road Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of Tayota Glaza car bearing No.KA-53-MJ-1166 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337, 304(A) of IPC.
Ex.P.3 is the certified copy of inquest.
Ex.P.4 is the certified copy of statement.
Ex.P5 and 6 are the Spot mahazar and sketch, which shows that the concerned police have drawn Mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P.7 is the certified copy of PM report, which shows that death is due to multiple injuries sustained.
Ex.P.8 is the IMV Report, which shows that accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the offending vehicle.
Ex.P.9 is the certified copy of aadhar card of deceased.

Ex.P.10 is the death report,
Ex.P.11 and 12 are the receipts and Ex.P.13 is the certified copy of the Charge-sheet, which shows that the I.O of Magadi Road Traffic Police Station has submitted Charge-sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 338, 304(A) of IPC.
13.
PW1 is subjected for cross examination by the learned counsel for Respondent No.1.

During his cross examination he has denied all the suggestions made by the counsel for respondent No.1.
14.
The respondents have not adduced any evidence to rebut the evidence of petitioner No.1.
Moreover, the charge sheet is the material document, which is not challenged by the driver of the offending vehicle.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence Alla Bakash vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150103006/
5 adduced by the Petitioner No.1 and the documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the Petitioners have proved that the said accident has occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car bearing No.KA-53-MJ-1166 and in the said accident, the mother of petitioners had sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

sentences.text: Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is in the "Affirmative".

Issue No. 1 and 3:
15.
Both these issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid the repetition of the facts.
16. It is stated in the Petition that the Petitioner No.1, 4 and 6 are the sons and Petitioner No.2, 3 and 5 are the daughters of the deceased.

In order to prove this fact, PW 1 has produced Ex.P.9 i.e.,
Aadhar Card of the deceased Hasina @ Hasina Taj.
Upon going through the said documents, the aadhar card at Ex.P.9 and contents of police papers do fortify the said fact.
Hence, the petitioners have proved that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Hasina @ Hasina Taj.

Therefore, the Petitioners are considered as the dependents of the deceased Hasina @ Hasina Taj.
17.
In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 50 years and her avocation is shown as vegetables and fruits street vendor and was earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month.

In this regard,
petitioners have not produced any documents to prove her avocation.
Therefore, in the absence of any income proof, this Tribunal is of the opinion that notional income has to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Since the accident has been occurred in the year 2023, the notional income has to be taken at Rs.16,000/- p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
18. Further, the Petitioners stated the age of the deceased Hasina @ Hasina Taj as 50 years at the time of the accident.
As per Aadhar card of the deceased Hasina @ Hasina Taj i.e., Ex.P.9, the date of birth of Hasina @ Hasina Taj was shown as 10.05.1962.
The alleged accident was occurred on 31.01.2023.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased Hasina @ Hasina Taj was 61 years.
Hence, the age of the deceased Hasina @ Hasina Taj to be taken at 61 years for the purpose of Assessment of compensation.
19. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
20.
The deceased has left behind her, sons and daughters.
Hence, the Petitioner No.1 to 6 are considered as dependents.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others).

sentences.text: Wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that : "Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/-, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/- and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/-".

The aforesaid amounts should be Alla Bakash vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150103006/
6 enhanced @ 10% in every three years."

sentences.text: The Petitioner No.1, 4 and 6 are the sons of the deceased and petitioner No.2, 3 and 5 are daughters of the deceased.
The children, have to live remaining part of their life in the absence of their mother.
The loss of mother full of hopes for the future can never be suitably compensated to a mother.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 to 6 are entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- each under the head of loss of consortium and Rupees 16,500/- towards loss of estate and Rupees 16,500/- towards funeral expenses.

II. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION:
21. Petitioner No.1 to 6 are the children and they lost their mother's love and care.
Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:
22. The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.10,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDENCY:
23.

It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased was notionally fixed at Rs.16,000/- p.m.
24.
In the case on hand the deceased was aged 61 years.
Her income is taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m.
As per dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2017 SC 5157, the deceased is not entitled to future prospects as she was aged more than 61 years.
The deceased died leaving behind 6 dependents.
In the judgment relied by the learned counsel for the petitioner Segaran.

V (supra) Hon'ble High court of Karnataka has followed the ration laid down in the case A.Manvalgan Vs A.Krishnamurthy &
others reported in ILR 2004 Kar.3268 and held that the claimants are entitled 1/3 rd of the income of the deceased and 2/3rd of income of deceased is required to be deducted towards her personal expenses.

sentences.text: Keeping in the mind of said ratio it is assessed.
After deducting 2/3rd of the amount towards personal expenses of deceased in Rs.16,000/- it comes to Rs.5,334/- (Rs.16,000 - Rs.10,666 = Rs.5,334/-) which is rounded up as Rs.5,300/-.
25. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.5,300/- p.m. and the multiplier '7' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.4,45,200/- (Rs.5300 X 12 X 7).
Considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.4,45,200/- under the head of loss of dependency.
26. TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED:

Thus, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.8,02,200/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.
27. Regarding Liability :
As already discussed in the Issue No.2, in this case the driver of the offending Tayota Glaza car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-MJ-1166 was charge-sheeted.
Further, there is no dispute about the validity of the Insurance Policy of the offending vehicle as on the date of accident.
Therefore, Respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, Respondent No.2 being the owner are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is in the "Affirmative" and Issue No. 3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
28. Issue No.4 : From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.8,02,200/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.8,02,200/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
However, Respondent No.1 being the insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount as stated supra with interest at the rate of 6% p.a within 60 days from the date of this award.

In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 50 years and her avocation is shown as vegetables and fruits street vendor and was earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month.
In this regard,
petitioners have not produced any documents to prove her avocation.
Therefore, in the absence of any income proof, this Tribunal is of the opinion that notional income has to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Since the accident has been occurred in the year 2023, the notional income has to be taken at Rs.16,000/- p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
The children, have to live remaining part of their life in the absence of their mother.
The loss of mother full of hopes for the future can never be suitably compensated to a mother.
The deceased died leaving behind 6 dependents.

After deducting 2/3rd of the amount towards personal expenses of deceased in Rs.16,000/- it comes to Rs.5,334/- (Rs.16,000 - Rs.10,666 = Rs.5,334/-) which is rounded up as Rs.5,300/-.
25. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.5,300/- p.m. and the multiplier '7' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.4,45,200/- (Rs.5300 X 12 X 7).
